summary.text: CA9 has the broadest convergent support of any candidate. It ranks 1 in the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197), is up at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712, padj 2.58e-30) and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787). Single-cell data place 0.976 of its transcripts in RCC cells, and clinical agents exist (girentuximab PHASE_3). It is not prognostic (TCGA Cox log HR -0.009) and ccRCC lines do not depend on it, so it is a surface, imaging and conjugate target rather than a dependency.

The target profile is led by SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, NNMT, CD70 and ENPP3, all up in tumour at RNA and protein and replicated in TCGA. Of these, NNMT, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 also replicate at protein level in the confirmatory DIA cohort (NNMT log2FC 4.776, SCARB1 2.334, SLC16A3 3.551). NNMT is the best-supported target-and-biomarker beyond CA9: it is tumour-cell derived in two single-cell datasets, not infiltration-driven, and higher expression is linked to worse survival (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479).

The biomarker profile is dominated by proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour. PSAT1 (protein log2FC -1.963, confirmatory -3.946) and PCK1 (confirmatory -4.819) replicate strongly, and ALDH6A1, SLC6A19 and ALDOB carry prognostic signal in TCGA where higher expression goes with better survival. These are lineage-loss markers, not drug targets.

The main disagreements concern cell of origin. CD70 ranks 2 of 2017 for antibody-drug-conjugate suitability, but its single-cell attribution does not replicate (T_NK in Li 2022, RCC in Zhang 2021), and SCARB1 is myeloid in one dataset and RCC in the other. The clinically validated axis, VHL loss and HIF-2alpha (belzutifan approved), is not captured by the expression-driven top ranks, and EPAS1 transcripts are mostly stromal in single-cell data.

omics.text: Among up-regulated candidates, CA9 (RNA log2FC 6.312, protein 2.269), CD70 (RNA 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279), ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544) and SCARB1 (RNA 2.974, protein 1.837) agree across RNA and protein in CPTAC. FABP6 is also up (RNA 4.006) but has a CNV gain frequency of 0.573, so part of the increase is a dosage effect.

The down-regulated side is tubule identity loss: PSAT1 (RNA log2FC -3.867, protein -1.963), ALDH6A1 (RNA -3.399, protein -1.925, CNV loss frequency 0.355 with cis rho 0.525) and SLC6A19 (RNA -4.574, protein -1.48). The founding drivers are visible at the genomic layer: VHL is mutated in 247 of 511 tumours and PBRM1 in 185 of 511, both with 3p loss in about 0.8 of CPTAC tumours.

literature.text: Literature in the corpus supports the leading up-regulated candidates but mostly through single-study or preclinical work. CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept discrimination of ccRCC that still needs prospective validation; CD70 is described as overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression and is being developed as a radiotracer target; NNMT is reported as a prognostic biomarker with selective inhibitors available, though not ccRCC-specific.

Some literature contradicts the expression direction: MT1G is low in tumour yet high expression is linked to poorer prognosis, PFKP is up in tumour but low expression goes with worse survival, and ABAT is called tumour-suppressive yet a poor-prognosis marker. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the densest mechanistic literature (overexpressed in over 90% of ccRCCs) but only preclinical support. SCARB1 and ENPP3 have strong omics support but almost no literature in this corpus, which is a gap rather than evidence against them.

external.text: Open Targets confirms clinical tractability for CA9 (girentuximab PHASE_3) and CD70 (cusatuzumab PHASE_2), both membrane proteins in UniProt, but ccRCC lines depend on neither, so they suit antibody, imaging or immune approaches. SCARB1 has predicted tractability only and no drugs. NNMT has no listed drugs, and its external case rests on prognosis.

The established targets sit outside the expression-driven top ranks. EPAS1 has an approved drug (belzutifan) and a selective but partial dependency (selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of 24 lines dependent, padj 0.061). MTOR is a dependency in all 24 ccRCC lines but is common essential, so toxicity is a concern. VHL and PBRM1 are the top Open Targets associations (0.6466 and 0.6348) and act as mechanism, not direct targets.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of tissue transcripts, tumour-cell versus proximal-tubule log2FC is 7.739 (padj 0.0189), and the RCC attribution replicates in a second single-cell dataset (tumour share 0.981). NNMT is RCC-dominant in both datasets (tumour share 0.97 and 0.948). MET and EGFR are mainly tumour-cell expressed, but MET versus tubule is not significant (padj 0.069) and EGFR is also present in proximal tubule.

Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CD74 and CXCR4 are immune genes (CD74 RNA log2FC at purity 1 only 0.561), and EPAS1 transcripts sit mostly in endothelium (0.365) with RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 0.46. CD70 and SCARB1 have conflicting attribution between the two single-cell datasets (CD70 T_NK versus RCC; SCARB1 Myeloid versus RCC), so their tumour-cell origin is uncertain.

spatial.text: In Visium, CA9 expression is attributed to RCC spots (composition-corrected share 0.999). Neighbours of high-CA9 spots are enriched in RCC (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017) and, less, in macrophages (0.099), so the CA9 niche is mostly tumour-on-tumour with some macrophage contact.
KDR expression in Visium is explained by endothelial spots (composition-corrected share 0.99), confirming it as a vascular microenvironment target rather than a tumour-cell one.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank pockets only and do not show that any degrader exists. Among candidates, KDR has a high site score (0.841, 7 accessible lysines) but modest ligand-site recall (0.4) and an endothelial target cell; CA9's best site is modest (0.546, pocket volume 126.8 A3); GAL3ST4 has a deep, well-modelled pocket (0.7874, 819.7 A3) without ligand-site validation; and COL23A1's model is too poor for a campaign (mean pLDDT 58.91).

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the leading first-in-class candidate (novelty 0.767): RCC cells hold 0.881 of tumour transcripts, it has no clinical drug, it is surface or secreted with low vital-organ expression (max nTPM 3), and it replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives purity extrapolation (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88). RAB42 follows (novelty 0.705, TCGA log2FC 4.371, purity-1 log2FC 3.189).

The stroma and immune tracks are weaker. OLFML2A is a fibroblast candidate (0.647 of tumour transcripts) but reaches nTPM 27.9 in colon. GAL3ST4 is a macrophage gene (0.972 of transcripts) whose RNA log2FC at purity 1 is only 0.401 and which is adverse in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.177); LILRB4 is infiltration-driven (purity-1 log2FC 0.508 versus TCGA 3.7).

All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. None is a selective DepMap dependency (COL23A1 mean effect 0.167, RAB42 -0.075), none has functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.

validation.text: External replication and purity checks strengthen CA9 (TCGA log2FC 9.712, purity-1 log2FC 7.787), CD70 (TCGA 7.09, purity-1 4.278), NNMT (TCGA 4.685, purity-1 5.256) and SCARB1 (TCGA 3.989, purity-1 3.762): their bulk increases are tumour-intrinsic, not infiltration. They weaken immune genes such as CD74 (purity-1 log2FC 0.561) and LILRB4. NNMT is the only up-regulated leader with an adverse prognosis signal (Cox padj 0.00479).

In the confirmatory DIA cohort, protein calls replicate for NNMT (log2FC 4.776, padj 3.07e-46), SCARB1 (2.334), SLC16A3 (3.551), PSAT1 (-3.946) and PCK1 (-4.819). CA9 and CD70 were not testable there (too few matched pairs), which is not a failure to replicate. Single-cell replication supports CA9, NNMT and PCK1, but not CD70, SCARB1 or PSAT1.

Somatic driver status and dependency point elsewhere: VHL (247 of 511 tumours) and PBRM1 (185 of 511) are the recurrent drivers, and EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective partial dependency (selectivity 0.3). None of the expression-ranked surface targets is a ccRCC dependency.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting, the target-profile leaders are stable: SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1 to 8) and CA9 (p_top10 0.941, 1 to 13), followed by SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 (0.88), NNMT (0.88) and ENPP3 (0.823). In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 is the most robust (p_top10 0.986, interval 1 to 4), with PCK1 (0.889) and SLC6A19 (0.881).

In the overall ranking only CA9 is a robust top-10 gene (p_top10 0.894, p_top25 0.983). Other positions depend on the weights: VHL's interval spans 1 to 580 (p_top10 0.391) because it relies on the genetics stream alone, and immune genes such as FCER1G (p_top10 0.054) rank high only when omics weight dominates.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150 no leading candidate has a significant treatment association after correction. CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log HR per SD -0.383, padj 0.166) and on sunitinib (-0.262, padj 0.434); CA9 trends the same way (sunitinib -0.336, padj 0.332). No gene separates the two main arms: the arm differences are -0.121 for CD70 (padj 0.927) and 0.224 for CA9 (padj 0.779).

PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (0.22, padj 0.572) and PSAT1 likewise (0.164, padj 0.829). NNMT and EPAS1 returned only the 16-patient nivolumab trial, which is too small to interpret.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup candidate: mutant minus wild-type is 0.971 in CPTAC RNA (padj 0.014) and 1.148 in TCGA RNA, but the protein difference (0.335, padj 0.067) is not significant, and CA9 is lower in ccB than ccA. PSAT1 tracks the aggressive ccB state (TCGA RNA 2.364, padj 9.07e-39) rather than a single mutation. NNMT shows no mutation or ccA/ccB difference, so its increase is pan-subgroup.

SCARB1 is higher in PBRM1 mutants at RNA (TCGA 0.583) but not at protein (0.306, padj 0.113), and lower in BAP1 mutants. Subtype differences in bulk RNA can partly reflect infiltration, which matters for SCARB1 given its mixed single-cell attribution.

adc.text: CD70 is the best conjugate candidate on suitability (0.746, rank 2 of 2017) but has no staining data, so vital-organ safety cannot be judged. SLC16A3 scores 0.725 (rank 3) with the best coverage but only 66 extracellular residues across 12 transmembrane segments. SCARB1, top of the target profile, ranks only 51 (0.558) with low tumour-cell coverage.

The known controls behave as expected with caveats: CA9 scores 0.647 (rank 13) but stains at level 3.0 in stomach, and ENPP3 scores 0.578 (rank 39) with level 3.0 staining in duodenum and kidney. Heterogeneity is a shared problem, since only 24.3 percent of CA9-expressing tumour cells are seen in the weakest quarter of donors.

immune.text: FCER1G (immune share 0.999, rho 0.898 with the immune score) and FCGR3A (immune share 0.999) are immune-cell genes whose tumour-up signal reflects infiltration, linking them to hot tumours rather than tumour biology. CD70 is partly immune: immune cells make 0.654 of its tumour transcripts, conflicting with the tumour-cell reading. NNMT is the negative control here (immune share 0.015), so its increase is independent of how hot or cold the tumour is.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9 and CD70 as surface targets and on NNMT as a target-and-biomarker; for NNMT, prognosis, confirmatory protein and single-cell replication all agree. They disagree on SCARB1 (strong omics and confirmatory protein, almost no literature, no drugs, mixed cell attribution) and on CD70's cell of origin. Tubule-loss genes (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC6A19) are the biomarker layer, while VHL, PBRM1 and EPAS1 are mechanism and validated-therapy context.

targets.rationale: Overall convergence rank 1 and target profile p_top10 0.941. Tumour-intrinsic in two single-cell datasets, replicates in TCGA (log2FC 9.712) and holds at purity 1; girentuximab reached PHASE_3. No dependency and no prognostic signal, so it is a surface, imaging and conjugate target.

Up at RNA and protein, confirmatory protein log2FC 4.776, RCC-dominant in both single-cell datasets, not immune-derived, and adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301). Placed above the numeric target order because every independent layer agrees; selective inhibitors exist but no ccRCC drug.

Strong omics (protein log2FC 2.421, TCGA 7.09), clinical antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2) and ADC suitability rank 2 of 2017. Held below NNMT because its single-cell attribution does not replicate and immune cells make 0.654 of its transcripts.

Top of the target profile (score 4.1314, p_top10 0.968) and protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort (2.334). Placed fourth here because it has no drugs, little literature, mixed single-cell attribution (Myeloid versus RCC) and an ADC suitability rank of only 51.

MCT4 lactate exporter, up at RNA (3.435) and protein (2.279), replicates in the confirmatory cohort (3.551), and target-profile p_top10 0.881. ADC suitability rank 3 but antibody access is limited by its small extracellular surface.
Membrane enzyme up at RNA (3.895) and protein (1.544) with TCGA log2FC 5.557, and an ADC (AGS-16C3F) reached PHASE_2. Its level 3.0 staining in duodenum and kidney is a safety concern.

The validated ccRCC target (belzutifan approved) with a selective partial dependency (selectivity 0.3). It sits outside the expression-driven ranks because its RNA signal is mostly stromal (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 0.46); included as the clinical benchmark.

Most robust biomarker-profile gene (p_top10 0.986), protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort (-3.946), and it is prognostic in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.43). Associated with the ccB state; single-cell attribution is inconsistent.
Proximal-tubule gene whose protein loss replicates strongly (confirmatory log2FC -4.819) and which is RCC-dominant in both single-cell datasets; biomarker-profile p_top10 0.889.
Down at RNA (-3.399) and protein (-1.925) with a real dosage effect from 14q loss (cis rho 0.525), and strongly prognostic (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12).
Overall convergence rank 2 on the biomarker side: down in tumour (TCGA log2FC -4.741), literature support as a prognostic marker, and higher expression linked to better survival (Cox log HR -0.358).
Tubule transporter lost in tumour (RNA log2FC -4.574) with strong prognostic signal (Cox log HR -0.456, padj 1.07e-7) and biomarker-profile p_top10 0.881.

limitations.text: All evidence is associative; no candidate has functional validation in this analysis, and none of the surface targets is a ccRCC dependency.
CA9 and CD70 could not be tested in the confirmatory protein cohort, and HK2 (target-profile top 10) was not queried for confirmatory replication in this run, so its protein call is unconfirmed.
Single-cell attribution disagrees between datasets for CD70, SCARB1 and PSAT1, and the second dataset has few paired donors.
IMmotion150 arms have about 90 patients each; treatment associations are leads, and no gene separates the arms after correction.
Literature relations come from an LLM extractor over a limited abstract set; absence of literature is not absence of published work.
Phosphosite and kinase-activity layers and STRING interactions were not queried by the agents in this run.
Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank candidate pockets only and are not evidence that a degrader exists.
